headline: Bullpen implodes as Mets rout Phillies 10-3
recap: The Phillies fell 10-3 to the Mets at Citi Field on Saturday. Carson Benge opened the scoring with a solo home run in the second. Philadelphia answered in the fourth when Alec Bohm's single brought home Bryce Harper, then briefly led in the fifth on Bryce Harper's sacrifice fly that scored Kyle Schwarber and another Bohm single that plated Trea Turner. New York took the lead for good later in the fifth when Francisco Alvarez hit a three-run homer off Andrew Painter, who took the loss (3-10) despite seven strikeouts across 5.1 innings. The Mets tacked on two more in the sixth on a Brett Baty single and a bases-loaded walk to Ronny Mauricio, then broke the game open with four runs in the eighth off Orion Kerkering, who was charged with all four, on RBI hits and walks from Francisco Lindor, Juan Soto, Bo Bichette and Benge, who finished 3-for-4 with the homer. Trea Turner reached base four times (2-for-3, two walks, a stolen base) and Alec Bohm drove in two.
The Phillies are 85-70, in second place in the NL East, 6.0 games behind the first-place Braves, and have lost two straight.

Philadelphia closes its series at Citi Field this afternoon, with Cristopher Sánchez opposing Mets right-hander Jonah Tong; first pitch is scheduled for 1:10 PM ET. DraftKings has the Phillies as -171 favorites (Mets +141), with Philadelphia -1.5 (+101) on the run line. An off day follows Monday before the Phillies open a three-game series at home against the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday.
